notes: Verify the current API version, key requirements, rate limits, paging behavior, and supported response formats.
Do not store API keys or credentials in this manifest.
Record method names, parameters, identifiers, response fields, error semantics, examples, and deprecation notices.
Distinguish API metadata from IIIF manifests, image services, bulk exports, OAI-PMH, and website download interfaces.
Capture exact official legal wording and item-level rights statements before normalizing rights metadata.
Separate bibliographic metadata, OCR text, page images, complete works, IIIF resources, and third-party identifiers.
Public-domain status and reuse permissions may differ by jurisdiction, item, contributor, and underlying work.
Do not assume consortium-level openness overrides item-specific restrictions or contributor statements.
Do not assume source-code licensing applies to metadata, OCR, scans, page images, or complete works.
Seed URLs are best-effort and were not live-verified in this session.
The acquisition program should update retrieval, content, review, and verification fields in place.
Some service paths may redirect, be renamed, require API keys, or be unavailable; preserve redirect and failure metadata.
Do not recursively crawl every title, item, page, part, segment, image, author, collection, or contributor when the task is documentation acquisition.
Do not store API keys, passwords, cookies, OAuth tokens, or session credentials in this JSON file.
Bibliographic metadata, OCR, scientific-name indexes, page images, complete works, IIIF resources, and source code may carry different rights.
Always preserve item-level rights statements, contributor attribution, persistent identifiers, and source provenance.
